description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, y-axis) for six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—used to edit large language models for long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, spans from 40% to 65% in linear increments of 5%. The “Base” method (black solid line with circular markers) starts at ~40% ACC at low co-occurrence and plateaus near 44% as co-occurrence increases. “FT” (blue line with downward-pointing triangles) begins at ~42% and rises gradually to ~48%. “IKE” (red line with upward-pointing triangles) starts at ~43% and increases to ~49.5%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~44% and rises steadily to ~56.5%. “MEMIT” (purple line with circular markers) starts at ~44% and climbs to ~55%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) begins at ~51% and shows the steepest increase, reaching ~66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All lines exhibit a generally upward trend, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the full range.
